text:
The niece has a fee simple, because the conveyance to the cousin created only a life estate (or fee tail converted to fee simple in the cousin under modern law), leaving nothing for the grantor to convey to the niece; however, if the cousin’s interest is treated as a fee tail that becomes a fee simple in the cousin, the niece gets nothing. Under the most common modern rule, the cousin holds a fee simple, so the niece has no interest.  
CONFIDENCE: 85
